subject: Social Media
title: Metadata Tells All
description: A quick, practical guide to Metadata Tells All.

hook.text: The NSA said: 'We kill people based on metadata.' Not content—just who called whom, when, and from where.

buildup.text: Metadata is data about data: timestamps, locations, durations, recipients. It doesn't include the actual message.

discovery.text: A call to a suicide hotline at 3 AM reveals more than any text message could. Patterns expose intent.

twist.text: Companies claim they don't read your messages. They don't need to. Metadata tells the story without the words.

climax.text: Metadata is collected at massive scale with no warrant. Courts treat it as less private than content. It isn't.

punchline.text: They don't need your words. The patterns are enough.

quiz.question: Why is metadata considered so revealing?
options: Patterns of communication reveal intent and relationships
